headline: Galápagos Sea Turtles Defy Expectations by Staying Close to Home
meta_description: Scientists tracking yellow-morph green sea turtles in the Galápagos discovered they prefer staying near their islands rather than roaming the ocean.
summary_short: A surprising population of Galápagos sea turtles stayed within the marine reserve instead of making long ocean journeys, revealing the islands' crucial role in their sur…
body:
Scientists studying yellow-morph green sea turtles in the Galápagos made an unexpected discovery: these creatures, renowned for extraordinary ocean journeys, actually prefer staying remarkably close to home. Over three years of satellite tracking, none of the nine tagged turtles—including individuals nicknamed Bernardo, Sara, and the most adventurous, Ainoa—left the 198,000 square kilometer Galápagos Marine Reserve. Most spent their time in shallow coastal waters, rarely venturing more than a few kilometers from shore. This finding challenges what researchers thought they knew about these particular turtles, which are one of two genetically distinct forms of green sea turtles living in the archipelago.

The tracking study, led by Dr. John W. Rowe from Alma College, revealed that individual turtles maintained home ranges averaging 1,498 square kilometers, with most staying near a single island. Only during the cooler months from April through October did some turtles move between islands. The researchers emphasized that female yellow morphs likely do eventually migrate to western Pacific breeding grounds not yet documented in the Galápagos, suggesting this snapshot captures only part of their life cycle.

The discovery carries important lessons for conservation. Because these turtles depend on routes and habitats across multiple islands, protecting single feeding locations isn't enough. Instead, researchers stress the need to preserve coastal waters and inter-island passages throughout the entire archipelago. The finding underscores how critical the Galápagos' marine ecosystem is to these turtles' survival—and why maintaining that habitat intact matters for the species' future.
quick_facts: Nine adult yellow-morph green sea turtles tracked for up to 418 days
None left the 198,000 sq km Galápagos Marine Reserve during the study
Most turtles stayed within shallow coastal waters near single islands
Seasonal movement between islands occurred only April through October
Each turtle used home range averaging 1,498 square kilometers
